title: Storage backend: SQL or KV on the object (elicited)
context: A Cloudflare Durable Object exposes state.storage per https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/. Two backends are documented: SQL storage (state.storage.sql) supports typed columns and query; KV storage (state.storage.put/get/delete/list) is simpler and single-key. Both are useful; the choice depends on the shipped object's data shape. The elicit forces the operator to pick at apply time so the shipped code path can carry the trace record.
decision: The applied blueprint elicits do-storage-backend at apply time with two options (sql, kv). The recommendedDefault is sql for new objects (SQL supports typed columns and future migrations without a driver rewrite). The chosen answer threads through the storage driver factory as driver.backend per AC-33111-1; the shipped SingleCellObject class code is backend-agnostic and does not care which backend is live.
consequences: A project that picks sql inherits the DO SQL storage semantics and the shipped SQL migration path; a project that picks kv inherits the simpler put/get/delete/list surface and the KV eventual-consistency-on-the-object trade the guide documents. Standards trace clause: generic enterprise practice (the sql-vs-kv trade is a general enterprise-tier storage-shape choice, not a Cloudflare-specific claim).
